title: Rotate-Register Kaleidoscope
desc: An 8-fold mandala driven by circular bit rotations: eight ring registers rotate at different constant speeds (__builtin_rotateleft8/right8), while a 16-bit outer word rotates by a runtime amount. Exercises G_ROTL/G_ROTR ConstantAmt path and S8 special case. Compiler stress-test #74.

heading: Rotate-Register Kaleidoscope
lede: An 8-fold-symmetric kaleidoscope on a Super Nintendo driven by circular bit rotations. Eight ring registers rotate at different constant speeds via __builtin_rotateleft8/rotateright8, exercising the llvm-mos ConstantAmt fast path and S8 special case in legalizeShiftRotate. A 16-bit outer word rotates by a runtime frame-derived amount, exercising the variable-amount lowering path. Compiler stress-test #74 — the first demo in the battery to use any rotate builtin.
keysHtml: Self-running demo — ring registers precess producing counter-rotating petals.
doc:
What it is

The screen is a 16×16 tile grid folded into 8-fold symmetry (octant reflection). Each tile belongs to one of 8 concentric rings (by Chebyshev distance from center). Every ring has a uint8_t register that rotates at its own constant speed — rings 0–3 rotate left at 1, 2, 3, 1 bits per frame; rings 4–7 rotate right at 1, 2, 3, 1 bits per frame. A uint16_t outer word rotates by a runtime-variable amount each frame. Two bits extracted from the ring register, XOR'd with the top two bits of the outer word, select one of four palette colours. Counter-rotating rings at incommensurable speeds produce moire interference patterns that continuously evolve without ever repeating. 

// 8 ring registers (uint8_t) + 1 outer word (uint16_t)
// Per-frame rk_step(s, k):

ring[0] = rotl8(ring[0], 1);  // constant amount — ConstantAmt path
ring[1] = rotl8(ring[1], 2);
ring[2] = rotl8(ring[2], 3);
ring[3] = rotl8(ring[3], 1);
ring[4] = rotr8(ring[4], 1);  // right rotate — S8 special case
ring[5] = rotr8(ring[5], 2);
ring[6] = rotr8(ring[6], 3);
ring[7] = rotr8(ring[7], 1);
outer   = rotl16(outer, k);   // k = (frame & 14)+1 — runtime amount

// Per-tile colour rk_cell(s, tx, ty):
ax = abs(dx); ay = abs(dy);         // center-relative
ox = min(ax,ay); oy = max(ax,ay);   // octant fold → 8-fold symmetry
ring_idx  = min(oy >> 3, 7);        // Chebyshev ring 0..7
ring_val  = (ring[ring_idx] >> (ox & 7)) & 3;  // 2 bits
outer_bits = (outer >> 14) & 3;                 // top 2 bits
colour = ring_val ^ outer_bits;     // 0..3 → 2bpp palette

Compiler stress-test

ItemWhat it exercises
G_ROTL / G_ROTRlegalizeShiftRotate at MOSLegalizerInfo.cpp:1029–1254 handles circular bit rotates. It branches on whether the shift amount is a compile-time constant (ConstantAmt fast path, :1046–1061), on the bit-width (S8 special case for 8-bit rotates, :1167–1178), and on the runtime-amount case. This demo fires all three sub-paths.
constant amounts__builtin_rotateleft8(ring[i], 1) with a literal "1" lets the compiler take the ConstantAmt fast path: it knows the exact displacement at compile time and can fold the rotate into a dedicated instruction sequence (ROL/ROR on the 65816, which natively rotate through the carry flag). Rings 0–3 rotate left, rings 4–7 rotate right, at different constant speeds.
S8 special caseThe 65816's ROL/ROR instructions operate through the carry flag, making them a 9-bit rotate. The S8 special case (line 1167) emits the correct CLC+ROL (or SEC+ROR) sequence to produce a pure 8-bit circular shift. This path had not been exercised by any prior demo.
runtime amount__builtin_rotateleft16(outer, k) where k = (frame & 14)+1 is a non-constant, so the compiler must emit a general variable-shift sequence — a shift loop or a combined shift+OR. The outer word's top 2 bits are XOR'd into each tile's colour, producing shimmering interference beats between rings.
integer-exact gateCircular rotates on fixed-width unsigned integers are pure bitwise operations — bit-identical host vs target, no rounding, no UB. Any wrong lowering (shifted by off-by-one, wrong direction, missing wrap) diverges the CRC immediately. GATE_N=100 (not a multiple of 8) avoids the state-period trap where multiples of 8 steps return all registers to their initial values and yield CRC=0.

Written in C with the llvm-mos 65816 toolchain and verified against bsnes-jg and MAME. Hit Verify fidelity to reproduce the build gate's WRAM assert (gate CRC 0x300C — 100-step rotating-XOR fold of all ring registers and outer word) live in this tab. No far pointers — host == default == +mos-a16 == +mos-xy16, -verify clean.
